issue.title: sessions: two agents told to share one folder under different spellings (a link, a letter's case on Windows) read its sessions twice: Pi and omp, Qoder and Qoder CN
issue.body:
Found while landing #2932's fix (CodeBuddy Code in WorkBuddy's folder).

#2932's fix keeps each path once in `allFiles` and `callSources` (`distinctPaths`), and reads CodeBuddy Code's folder as WorkBuddy's when `os.SameFile` says the two are one folder. The other pairs of agents that a variable can point at one folder only get the path-text dedup:

- Pi and omp: `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to omp's `~/.omp/agent` lists each `sessions/*/*.jsonl` from `piFiles` and `ompFiles`.
- Qoder and Qoder CN: `QODER_CONFIG_DIR` and `QODERCN_CONFIG_DIR` on one folder lists each file from both `ccFiles` calls.

When both spell the folder the same, `distinctPaths` keeps the first listing, so a session is read once (under the first agent's name). When the spellings differ (a symlink or junction, or `C:\Users\x\.qoder` beside `c:\users\x\.qoder` on Windows), the paths differ as text, so each session is listed twice, under both agents, and its calls are counted twice in usage. It no longer crashes: that was the duplicate path in one refresh, fixed in #2932.

Not reproduced with a real install; this is from reading `allFiles`, `piFilesIn`, `ompFilesUnder` and `QoderDir`. A fix would decide the agent for a shared folder as #2932 did for WorkBuddy (`sameFolder` in `internal/sessions/workbuddy.go`), or key the dedup on the file's identity instead of its path text.

issue.title: sessions: v0.1.1291 quits at start with "panic: close of nil channel" in refresh's publish

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

After updating to **v0.1.1291** (macOS arm64, Darwin 25.5), magpie quits every time a few seconds after start. It reproduces on every launch. Going back to **v0.1.1290** fixes it: that build has been running normally on the same data.

Run from a terminal, the binary exits with status 2:

```
panic: close of nil channel

goroutine 103 [running]:
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.refresh.func5(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/sessions.go:886
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.refresh(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/sessions.go:900 +0xe08
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.statsIn(0x0, ...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/stats.go:143 +0x430
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.StatsAndNative(0x0)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/stats.go:117 +0x68
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.combinedSessionStats(0x0)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:466 +0x48
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.statsFor(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:443 +0x2ac
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmSessions.func1.1.warmSteps.1()
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:507 +0x20
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmUp(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:529 +0x38
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmSessions.func1.1()
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:497 +0x50
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.Warm(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/quiet.go:31 +0x94
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmSessions.func1()
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:497 +0x30
created by github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmSessions in goroutine 1
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:493 +0x50
```

## Where it seems to come from

The panic is `close(parsing[j.f.path])` in `refresh`'s `publish` (sessions.go:886 at v0.1.1291). The `parsing` map arrived with c381e4cd ("a read is never held by another read's refresh…", #2776), which is in 1291 and not in 1290.

For `parsing[path]` to be nil at publish time, its entry has to be deleted already. As far as I can see, only `publish` deletes entries. So probably the same path is published twice: either it is in `todo` twice in one refresh (the `parsing[f.path] != nil` check runs before any entry is set, so a duplicate in `want` gets past it and its channel is overwritten), or another refresh published it in between. I could not tell which file triggers it. A rough re-implementation of the listings for the agents on this machine found no duplicate paths, but that was not the real `allFiles()`. Agents with sessions here: Claude Code, Codex (incl. `.jsonl.zst` in archived_sessions), Grok, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy Code, Pi, Cursor (agent-transcripts only), dsh, and Hermes (root `state.db` plus one named profile).

A guard against a duplicate path in `todo` (or `publish` skipping a nil channel) would at least keep the warm-up from taking the whole app down.

issue.title: [Bug] panic: close of nil channel in sessions.refresh when PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR points to omp dir

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Environment
- OS: macOS (arm64)
- Magpie Version: 0.1.1318

### Description
When `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` is set to `~/.omp/agent` in the user's shell environment (which is commonly set by users or plugins migrating from Pi to Oh My Pi), Magpie desktop app and background daemon continuously panic on startup or during session warm-up:

```text
panic: close of nil channel

goroutine 102 [running]:
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.refresh.func5(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/sessions.go:891
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.refresh({0x4e5a9e1fa000?, 0x3d9, 0x1075b98a0?}, {0x4e5a9e1fa000, 0x3d9, 0x0?})
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/sessions.go:905 +0xe08
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.statsIn(0x0, {0xc2ae939f1928f2d0?, 0xbedec890?, 0x1075b98a0?}, 0x4e5a9cc36d50)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/stats.go:143 +0x430
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.StatsAndNative(0x0)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/stats.go:117 +0x68
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.combinedSessionStats(0x0)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:466 +0x48
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.statsFor(0x1045b0340?)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:443 +0x2ac
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmSessions.func1.1.warmSteps.1()
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:507 +0x20
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmUp(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:529 +0x38
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui.warmSessions.func1.1()
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gui/sessions.go:497 +0x50
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions.Warm(...)
	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/sessions/quiet.go:31 +0x94
```

### Root Cause
1. In `internal/sessions/pi.go`:
   `PiDir()` respects `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. When `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` points to `~/.omp/agent`, `piFiles()` collects session files under `~/.omp/agent/sessions/`.
2. In `internal/sessions/omp.go`:
   `OmpDir()` defaults to `~/.omp/agent`, and `ompFiles()` collects session files from the exact same directory.
3. In `internal/sessions/sessions.go:allFiles()`:
   Files from both `piFiles()` and `ompFiles()` are appended together into `out []file` without path deduplication.
4. In `internal/sessions/sessions.go:refresh()`:
   Duplicate `f.path` entries are appended into `todo` slice, resulting in multiple concurrent jobs targeting the exact same file path.
5. In `publish(i int)`:
   When worker 1 finishes, it runs:
   ```go
   close(parsing[j.f.path])
   delete(parsing, j.f.path)
   ```
   When worker 2 finishes for the duplicate file, `parsing[j.f.path]` is `nil`. Closing a nil channel immediately triggers `panic: close of nil channel`.
6. Furthermore, on macOS desktop launches, `proc.UserPath()` queries the user's interactive login shell (`zsh -ilc`), detects `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, and injects it into Magpie's environment, causing the desktop app to crash even when launched from Finder/Dock.

### Suggested Fix
1. In `internal/sessions/sessions.go` -> `refresh()`, deduplicate file paths when building `todo`:
   ```go
   seen := make(map[string]bool, len(want))
   for _, f := range want {
       if f.cold || seen[f.path] {
           continue
       }
       seen[f.path] = true
       // ...
   ```
2. Defensively guard channel closing in `publish()`:
   ```go
   if ch := parsing[j.f.path]; ch != nil {
       close(ch)
       delete(parsing, j.f.path)
   }
   ```

issue.title: sessions: a Claude Code project folder reachable under two names in projects/ (a link left after moving the project) is counted once per name; usage counts it once

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### magpie version

v0.1.4087

### Where

CLI (`magpie sessions`). I have not compared the Sessions page in the GUI.

### OS

macOS 15

### Agent, provider and model

Claude Code (session files read directly, no gateway involved)

### Steps to reproduce

Two entries in `~/.claude/projects/` that resolve to the same folder: the real project folder, and a symlink left under the old name after the project was moved (so sessions started from the old path still land in the same history).

Minimal reproduction in a throwaway `HOME`, with one real Claude Code project folder copied in:

```
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/.claude/projects"
cp -R ~/.claude/projects/<some-project> "$T/.claude/projects/-tmp-proj"
export HOME="$T"
magpie sessions read on claude

magpie sessions --days 7 --json      # (1) real folder only
ln -s -- -tmp-proj "$T/.claude/projects/-tmp-alias"
magpie sessions --days 7 --json      # (2) one link to it
ln -s -- -tmp-proj "$T/.claude/projects/-tmp-alias2"
magpie sessions --days 7 --json      # (3) two links to it
magpie usage --csv --days 7          # (4) same three entries
```

### What happened, and what you expected

`magpie sessions` counts the folder once per name. `magpie usage` counts it once.

| | output tokens | cache read | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) real folder only | 1,118,814 | 554,498,529 | $174.61 |
| (2) + one link | 2,237,628 | 1,108,997,058 | $349.22 |
| (3) + two links | 3,356,442 | 1,663,495,587 | $523.83 |
| (4) `usage --csv`, three entries present | 1,118,814 | | |

All three rows are reported under the same folder name, so nothing in the output hints that the same files were read more than once.

Expected: (2) and (3) equal (1), as `usage` already does.

On my real machine one project has two such links, and `sessions --days 7` reported about $7,300 where `usage --days 7` reported about $3,800. Per folder: folders with no link matched a by-hand count of the transcripts (deduplicated by message id) exactly; the folder with two links came out at 3.15x.

This looks like the other side of #2268: since v0.1.1247 a link inside `projects/` is followed (which is right: before that the project vanished), but when its target is itself an entry of the same `projects/`, both names are walked. #3258 describes the same root cause for two agents sharing a folder (dedup keyed on path text rather than on the file's identity); this is the single-agent case, and here only `sessions` is affected.

### Note for anyone with the same layout

If you moved a project and left a symlink in `~/.claude/projects/` from the old encoded path to the new one, the Sessions totals for that project are multiplied by the number of names. Until this is fixed, read totals from `magpie usage`. Removing the link is not a good workaround if sessions are still started from the old path: Claude Code would start a separate history under that name.

### Error text or logs

```text
(none: silent wrong totals)
```
